scope: Three isolated headless Chrome development-package observations on one desktop. The first run diagnosed a disposal defect; the second repeated 20 cycles after its correction; the third records separate checkpoints at 20 and 40 cycles. Explicit garbage collection precedes each snapshot. No player wins or stored progress, radio input, installed PWA or physical-device evidence. No p95 or natural-pacing comparison.

diagnosis.before: A connected generated course button retained its onclick closure after app disposal, retaining the app renderer, Scene and WebGLRenderer. The wrapper API had already been released.
diagnosis.fix: Clear only app-owned generated course-button handlers and remove those owned buttons during disposal. Old generated handlers are also cleared on translation replacement. No engine or replay rule change.
diagnosis.after: The corrected runs have no Scene, WebGLRenderer, Group, CanvasTexture, frame or paint cohort members after disposal and wrapper-reference release. Host DOM remains mounted.
diagnosis.remainingLibraryObjectCaveat: Named cohorts also include module scratch objects and exported constructor prototypes. Only up to two paths per cohort were sampled; these are not an exhaustive classification of all remaining objects.

limitations: Shallow heap totals are not dominator/exclusive retained memory. Population stability does not prove total memory stability.
Forced GC and snapshots perturb the process; no natural runtime pacing claim.
No native decoder, browser-process RSS or GPU byte accounting.
Three renderer texture bookkeeping may retain 1 after disposal; actual WebGL contextLost=true is recorded without rewriting counters.
At most two shortest strong paths per named cohort are sampled; weak edges are excluded and missing detachedness would remain unknown.
Development-package source pins describe exact compiled bytes, not release admission or a committed-source build.
Raw heaps may include source and fixture strings and stay in ignored local evidence; only bounded hashes/counts/diagnosis are public.

observation.interpretation: The second forced-GC interval did not continue the first interval's shallow-byte growth in this run. This narrows the earlier growth concern but does not prove leak freedom or stable process/native/GPU memory.
